chapter_title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ... ]
chapter_note: A short, remarkably pure teaching chapter. The substrate maps word-production through five bodily members onto coin-production through five craftsmen — a classic both-sides-internal correspondence. Five-fold structure is the hallmark of the oldest teaching layer. The only editorial material is the brief dialogue frame attribution in ¶1. All NLP register scores are 0.0 because the vocabulary here (throat, tongue, teeth, lips, craftsmen, coin) falls outside the typical cosmic-entity keyword lists, but the STRUCTURE (five-fold systematic process mapping) is unmistakably substratic. Gardner's synopsis confirms the coin analogy as the chapter's core.

paragraphs.core_text: The production of the word t[hat comes] from the mouth and is heard by the [ears]. [ ... ⟨p.261⟩ ... ] and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips g[at]her it! The word shall come forth through the power of th[ese five] members and be heard outside.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again he speaks about' (dialogue frame formula) and 'He says' (dialogue attribution). Preserved the lacuna and substantive topic definition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with standard dialogue frame formula 'Once again he speaks about...' then 'He says'. The teaching itself is a five-fold body-process mapping: throat → tongue → teeth → lips → (implied fifth from lacuna, possibly the chest/lungs). This is systematic, impersonal, process-oriented — classic substrate voice. The five-member structure is the backbone of the oldest teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: Simila[rly] the coin: One shall pour it out and an [othe]r beat it and another trim it as it is turned, and a[nother] put the stamp on it and another wipe it in the sieve (?). [Behold], these five craftsmen shall shape and beautify [their] coin, and it comes amongst mankind. It becomes a posse[ssion] to be received and given.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure correspondential analogy: five craftsmen mapped to five stages of coin production, corresponding to the five bodily members that form the word. Both sides of the mapping stay within the system — body-process → craft-process. No editorial extension, no contemporary application, no exhortation. The 'Simila[rly]' is a teaching-internal connective linking the two halves of the correspondence, not an editorial bridge.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case with the [wor]d, as it is formed and embellished by five [member]s. It comes forth and is heard by the ears [of] others.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary closure that completes the correspondence by returning to the word-formation side. Impersonal, systematic voice. 'Five members' restates the structural principle. This is the teaching tying its own bow — not editorial addition.
